domain: The critique of advertising's manipulation of desire — from Vance Packard's 'hidden persuaders' to today's algorithmic feeds — and whether the critique's own success has hollowed out its target
topic: The critique of advertising's manipulation of desire — from Vance Packard's 'hidden persuaders' to today's algorithmic feeds — and whether the critique's own success has hollowed out its target

movement.gist: Tell the triumph: mid-century critics (Packard-style) exposed advertising's psychological manipulation; the industry publicly absorbed the critique, adopting transparency codes and self-aware irony, seeming to concede defeat.

Show the object mutating across three slices: 1950s subliminal-persuasion ad, 1990s ironic/self-mocking ad that jokes about manipulating you, and today's algorithmic feed that doesn't persuade with a message at all but curates an environment of attention with no discrete ad to critique.

Stage the debate: some say the critique is obsolete since there is no longer a hidden persuader to unmask, everything is declared upfront; others insist the critique is needed more than ever, just retargeted — but the debate keeps citing the ironic-ad slice as if it were still the current target.

Deliver the lifecycle claim: critique doesn't die when its object confesses, it dies (or migrates) when its object stops being a message at all; the erosion of the artifact-level critique was necessary to expose that the real critique was always about structures of attention, not tricks of persuasion — this survivable core is what must be judged.

primary.axis: whether the critique of manipulative advertising remains valid once advertising itself has absorbed and neutralized that critique
poles: the critique is obsolete because its object confessed and rebranded
the critique is more necessary than ever because confession is itself a new technique of manipulation

secondary.axis: whether the unit of analysis should be the advertisement (a discrete manipulative message) or the environment (an ambient condition of attention)
poles: advertising as total ambient infrastructure of attention

tension_system.interaction: the primary debate about obsolescence turns out to be unanswerable at the level of the artifact, and the secondary axis — artifact versus environment — is what actually decides the verdict, so it displaces the original question as the one that matters

family_realization.note: Passage executes 'Moving Target' with precision. 1957-1994-2019 triptych keeps time-slices rigorously apart. Critique doesn't expire; it relocates. Artifactual charge erodes; attention-engineering claim survives. Difficulty realized: showing how obsolescence question itself becomes wrongly posed.

ending_behavior.note: 'Displacement' realized exactly. Original tension (does critique hold?) displaced by deeper tension (what stratum should the critique operate at?). 'The one now standing, and it is the one on which the verdict should turn' performs qualified resolution—displacement aperture clear.

voice_consistency.note: Cold Enthusiast sustained throughout. 'The wink' and 'filed his methods' show flat delivery of genuine fascination. One stubborn particular: the traffic network in Q4 grounds abstraction. Uneven polish: some sentences aphoristic, others deliberately syntactically complex. Avoids generic register.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1 (C) traps via example_promotion—plausible misread of 1994 as present condition. Q2 (D) traps via stance_misread—conflates author's framing with endorsement. Q3 (B) traps via stage_misattribution. Q4 (D) traps via stage_misattribution of where the durable claim locates. All require close reading of stratum logic.

explanation_quality.note: Every elimination names mechanism and passage location. 'stance_misread,' 'example_promotion,' 'scope_inflation,' 'level_confusion' are specific; cite paragraph/concept. No 'not mentioned.' Explanations trace why distractor fails at passage's own logic, not external standard.
